value.rationale: The exact moment-(in)determinacy boundary is a natural inference question for a shear-driven stationary displacement: even the complete hierarchy of moments loses uniqueness in any shear-sensitive direction, yet the transverse marginal remains uniquely characterized. The sharp tail and angular factor quantify rare flow-amplified excursions, distinguishing large deviations from Gaussian cores and elucidating nonuniformity of small-shear approximations. The fact is an all-parameter structural classification, not an arbitrary finite special case.
